label: Tensors: Multilinear Machines
notes: This chapter spans printed pages 304 through 326 and recasts tensors as inspectable multilinear machines. A tensor is a slot machine: feed it vectors and covectors, get back a number that is linear in each slot separately. Everything else this chapter builds rests on that single idea.

label: Multilinear Maps
notes: Multilinearity is linearity in one slot at a time, never joint linearity in all inputs together. We fix every argument but one and demand the leftover dependence be linear. This separate-slot structure is exactly what lets components on basis vectors reconstruct the whole map by expansion.

label: The Tensor Product of Spaces
notes: The abstract tensor product packages a bilinear map as a single linear map on a new space. Its universal property says every bilinear map factors uniquely through the tensor product. That is why tensors of type k,l are just multilinear functionals on copies of V and its dual.

label: Tensor Product of Tensors
notes: The tensor product of two tensors concatenates their slots: the first factor reads the first block of arguments, the second factor reads the rest. Elementary products of dual basis covectors give a basis for covariant tensors, so every tensor is a coordinate combination of these building blocks.

label: Covariant, Contravariant, Mixed
notes: Variance tracks which slots eat vectors and which eat covectors. Covariant slots take vectors, contravariant slots take covectors, and a mixed k,l tensor has both. The names anticipate how components respond to a change of basis, which is the transformation law we examine next.

label: Components and Transformation Law
notes: Components are the tensor evaluated on basis vectors and dual covectors. Change the basis and the components change by inserting the change-of-basis matrix into each lower slot and its inverse into each upper slot. The multilinear object is invariant; only its coordinate array shifts.

label: Eating Two Vectors
notes: Here is the picture to hold onto: a covariant 2-tensor is a grid that swallows two vectors and returns a scalar. The first vector selects a row weighting, the second a column weighting, and the component matrix B contracts them. Bilinearity is reading each input through its own slot.

label: Symmetric and Alternating
notes: Symmetrization and alternation are projection operators on tensors. The symmetric part averages over permutations of the arguments; the alternating part takes a signed average. Symmetric tensors ignore swaps, while alternating tensors flip sign and vanish whenever two arguments coincide, the seed of differential forms.

label: Splitting a 2-Tensor
notes: Any covariant 2-tensor splits cleanly into a symmetric and an alternating part: B equals half of B plus its transpose, plus half of B minus its transpose. The symmetric piece is a quadratic form, the skew piece a signed area, and together they reconstruct B exactly.

label: Tensor Fields on Manifolds
notes: A tensor field is a smooth section of a tensor bundle: one tensor attached to each tangent space, varying smoothly point to point. In a chart its components are smooth functions, and smoothness of the field is exactly smoothness of those coordinate component functions across the chart.

label: Operations on Tensor Fields
notes: Tensor fields support tensor product and contraction pointwise. Contraction pairs one upper slot with one lower slot and sums, lowering type by one and one. These operations are smooth, so they send smooth tensor fields to smooth tensor fields, building the full algebra of fields used later.

label: Pullback of Covariant Tensors
notes: Covariant tensors pull back along any smooth map by inserting its differential into every slot. For a 2-tensor this is the matrix sandwich J transpose times A composed with F times J. Crucially no inverse appears, so pullback needs no diffeomorphism, unlike pushing vectors forward.

label: Tensor Characterization Lemma
notes: The characterization lemma is the workhorse test. An operation on vector fields that is multilinear over smooth functions, not merely over constants, is automatically pointwise: it is a tensor field. Function-linearity in each slot is exactly the condition that the value at a point depends only on inputs at that point.

label: Recap and Takeaways
notes: To recap: tensors are multilinear machines, components are basis evaluations, tensor products build bases, symmetric and alternating projections split tensors, fields vary smoothly, covariant tensors pull back freely, and the characterization lemma certifies tensoriality. These threads converge next into differential forms and the exterior derivative.
